# Guided AI GRC Build: Proposal for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel (stated as budget holder)
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026 with Dana Whitfield, Ravi Okafor and Ingrid Solberg
**Program:** Guided AI GRC Build, 12 weeks, US$60,000

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. The company is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. It employs about 1,100 staff. The company describes itself as piloting AI and has three use cases at different stages:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

Several factors shape the work:

- **Internal audit finding.** An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that no inventory of AI systems exists.
- **Regulation.** The stated regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR.
- **Certification.** ISO/IEC 42001 is a certification target, with work to start next year. The start date is not fixed.
- **Sponsor objective.** Your stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."
- **Constraints.** Three constraints govern the work:
  - Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
  - Customer data must stay in the EU.
  - The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

Tamarack Instruments already operates an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and an ISO 9001 quality management system. These are management system foundations an AIMS should integrate with rather than duplicate. The specific registers, procedures and records within them are not yet confirmed and are treated as Unknown until Week 1.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Pure Consulting Delivery

A conventional consulting engagement typically delivers a finished document set to the Client. That approach can produce artifacts quickly. However, the knowledge of how they were built, and the habit of operating them, often leaves with the consultants.

The Guided AI GRC Build reverses this arrangement. Tamarack Instruments' own build team produces every artifact. Each week includes:

- one live virtual workshop to frame the work
- one coaching session to resolve the hard questions
- structured asynchronous implementation between sessions.

At Week 12 the Client holds a system it built, understands and can operate. This matters here for three reasons:

1. **The audit finding needs an owned process.** The finding concerns the absence of an inventory. An inventory maintained by people who did not build it tends to decay. An inventory the Client's own team built and owns is more likely to stay current.
2. **ISO/IEC 42001 readiness depends on internal ownership.** Readiness rests on demonstrated operation over time. The Client's team needs to run the processes before any certification work begins next year.
3. **Integration requires the people who know the incumbent systems.** Linking the AIMS to the existing ISMS and quality management system is best done by the people who operate those systems.

The program is grounded in three principles: **Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.** Concretely, every governed AI workflow built in the program names the human accountable for its outcomes.

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

### Inventory order for Weeks 2 to 5

Weeks 2 to 5 are anchored to the Client's actual use cases, in this order:

1. **Customer service chatbot (enters first).** It is the only use case stated as deployed, so it represents present operational exposure. It is assessed against GDPR and the EU data residency constraint.
2. **AI visual inspection pilot (enters first, alongside the chatbot).** It is the subject of the Sponsor's stated Q2 2027 objective. Its assessment must be complete before any production decision.
3. **AI sales forecasting (enters as a planned system).** It is recorded so that intake and assessment are in place before the system is built.

EU AI Act classification of each system is determined in Week 3 using the agreed methodology. **Confirm with external counsel.**

### Week-by-week plan

ISO/IEC 42001 themes in the table below indicate readiness alignment only. They do not represent a certification outcome.

| Week | Focus | Tailoring for Tamarack Instruments | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme | Incumbent integration point |
|---|---|---|---|---|

### Integration with incumbent frameworks

The Profile Block names the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and the ISO 9001 quality management system. It does not state which registers, procedures or records within them the AIMS would attach to. Every integration point is therefore marked Unknown. Week 1 confirms which incumbent artifacts exist so that integration points can be fixed for each week.

- **Slow AI Kitchen:** https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen
- **Board-layer reference, AI Governance for Boards:** https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The contracted outcome at Week 12 is a minimum viable AIMS comprising all six of the following elements:

1. An adopted charter.
2. A populated inventory.
3. An operating risk register.
4. An adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

**Delivery risk on element 5.** The customer service chatbot is the only use case stated as deployed. Whether the visual inspection pilot will be in production use by Week 12 is Unknown. The second governed workflow must therefore be identified and confirmed at the Week 1 steering checkpoint.

**Works council sequencing.** Any workflow that touches production staff is sequenced after German works council consultation. Whether the visual inspection workflow touches production staff is Unknown. **Confirm with external counsel.**

This outcome supports ISO/IEC 42001 readiness. It does not constitute or guarantee certification, a favorable audit result or regulatory compliance.

## 5. Client Team Commitment

All figures below are **estimates** of weekly hours per role. Actual effort will vary by week and is not yet known.

| Role | Estimated hours per week | Primary involvement |
|---|---|---|
| General Counsel | Estimate: 3 to 4 | Charter, policy adoption, regulatory classification, steering |
| CISO | Estimate: 3 to 5 | Risk methodology, supplier governance, incident response, ISMS integration |
| Head of Quality | Estimate: 4 to 6 | Procedures, lifecycle gates, change management, quality management system integration |
| Head of Data | Estimate: 4 to 6 | Inventory, impact assessments, data residency, monitoring |
| German plant manager | Estimate: 2 to 4, higher in Weeks 2, 4 and 9 | Visual inspection inventory, assessment and workflow |
| Internal auditor (each of two) | Estimate: 2 to 3 | Evidence design review, Week 11 evidence review, Week 12 walkthrough |

**Internal auditor independence.** We recommend that the two internal auditors act as reviewers rather than builders. This helps preserve their independence for future assurance work. The Client should confirm this approach at Week 1.

**Build team lead.** The build team lead is Unknown and should be named at Week 1.

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints are held at three points:

- **Week 1:** mobilization brief and decisions needed.
- **Week 6:** mid-point report, blockers and scope decisions.
- **Week 12:** closing report and minimum viable AIMS attestation.

Steering membership is Unknown and is confirmed at mobilization.

**Format.** Each week includes one live virtual workshop, one coaching session and structured asynchronous implementation between sessions.

**Timing against the Q2 2027 objective.** To support that objective, the start date should be set so that Week 12 concludes before visual inspection goes into production. The production date itself is stated only as Q2 2027.

**Price.** The price is US$60,000. This sits within the stated approved budget of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. Payment terms are Unknown and set out in the engagement agreement. **Confirm with external counsel.**
